name: MatterHackers, Inc.
summary: One of the largest US 3D-printing retailers, based in Lake Forest, California. MatterHackers is primarily a marketplace for third-party printers and materials — and owns/operates the LulzBot printer brand — but also sells house-brand filament under Pro Series (engineering tier) and MH Build Series (budget tier), claimed as made in the USA.

product_lines.name: MH Build Series (PLA / ABS / PETG)
product_lines.notes: Value-tier house brand of standard PLA, ABS and PETG resins; sold as 'MatterHackers Filament' before the MH Build Series rename.

product_lines.name: MH Build Series Silky PLA
product_lines.notes: Standard PLA plus a silk/pearlescent gloss additive.

product_lines.name: MH Build Series TPU
product_lines.notes: True thermoplastic polyurethane per MatterHackers' own spec sheet; shore hardness not published, so no durometer-specific id is assigned.

product_lines.name: ThriftyMake (PLA / PETG / ABS)
product_lines.notes: Lowest-cost house tier, positioned below MH Build Series; same base chemistries.

product_lines.name: PRO Series (PLA / ABS / PETG)
product_lines.notes: Professional tier: same base chemistries as MH Build Series with tighter tolerance/QC claims and US-manufacture claims.

product_lines.name: PRO Series Flex
product_lines.notes: Labelled TPE by MatterHackers, not TPU: shore 98A/50D, elongation ~600%, density 1.23 g/cm3, 235 C print temp; explicitly sold as a firmer alternative to NinjaFlex (85A TPU). Harder than the typical TPE grade behind the tpe entry.

product_lines.name: PRO Series Ryno
product_lines.notes: House-name 'professional-level copolyester' marketed as a PETG alternative; density 1.27 g/cm3 sits in the standard-PETG range but the formulation is undisclosed, so a petg mapping cannot be asserted.

product_lines.name: PRO Series NylonX
product_lines.notes: MatterHackers' own listing is titled 'NylonX Carbon Fiber PA12 Filament' — PA12 + chopped carbon fibre. This supersedes the additional_notes remark that NylonX is a third-party brand.

product_lines.name: PRO Series NylonG
product_lines.notes: Glass-fibre-infused nylon; PA type and GF loading undisclosed, so pa6-gf (provisional) cannot be asserted and the generic pa id is used for family context only.

product_lines.name: Ionic Hi-Temp Hybrid Support Material
product_lines.notes: Water/solvent-assisted support material; base chemistry not disclosed publicly, so it maps to neither pva nor bvoh nor hips.

product_lines.name: Third-party marketplace catalog
product_lines.notes: Hundreds of other brands resold (ColorFabb, Fillamentum, Polymaker and others), each originating wherever that brand manufactures. Not MatterHackers product.

additional_notes: manufacturing_countries covers the house brands only (US, per product-page claims). The wider marketplace is mixed/global by definition and should not be read as MatterHackers-origin. It is not established whether MatterHackers extrudes Pro Series / MH Build Series itself or contracts a US toll extruder; because no counterparty is named, no oem_relationships row is recorded. NylonX (carbon-fiber nylon) is a distinct third-party brand/manufacturer that MatterHackers retails, not a house brand — the full corporate relationship is unverified. Sells build plates and print surfaces, e.g. LayerLock Powder Coated PEI Build Plates (https://www.matterhackers.com/store/c/powder-coated-pei-build-plate); no plate entries exist in this catalog yet, so plate_ids is unset. Price tier spans budget (MH Build) to engineering (Pro Series PA-CF); "mid" is the midpoint of that span, not a measured position. HQ 20321 Valencia Cir, Lake Forest, CA.

provenance.conflicts: Whether house-brand filament is extruded in-house or by a contracted US toll extruder is unresolved; "Made in the USA" is a product-page claim with no primary-source manufacturing documentation. NylonX's status (third-party product carried vs. house line) is asserted from catalog context, not from a corporate statement. Price tier is a forced single value for a brand that deliberately spans budget to engineering.
